newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai stocks lose 3 pct on politics, baht.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai stocks lose 3 pct on politics, baht.

text.p: Thai stocks were hammered more than three percent on Monday on fears of internal squabbling within Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's New Aspiration Party (NAP) and sustained weakness of the baht.

The composite SET index fell for the third consecutive day, tumbling 18.91 points or 3.03 percent to 604.34 on thin 2.04 billion baht turnover. It was the indicator's lowest close since the baht was effectively devalued on July 2.

Brokers said a faction in NAP, led by Deputy Premier Sukavit Rangsitphol, raised market jitters after its elected members of parliament threatened on the weekend to rebel by withdrawing support for a government budget bill during parliamentary debates next month.
The NAP faction objected to Chavalit's decision on Friday to remove its members from cabinet posts after the prime minister announced a cabinet reshuffle.

"Investors lost confidence in the government, seeing the minor cabinet reshuffle last week of creating more squabbling among members in the coalition government," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance.
Chavalit brought in two outsiders to join his eight-month government as he tries to weather growing public criticism of the government's handling of the country's economic turmoil.
Analysts, however, did not expect the NAP faction to cause a serious problem for Chavalit. They said the uproar generated by the NAP faction should fade later this week.
The market was also hurt by tight liquidity and sustained weakness in the baht.

The baht faced renewed pressure amid continued weaknesss in other regional currencies. It fell sharply on a spillover of the rupiah's losses after Indonesia's move to float the rupiah. The rupiah hit a record low of 3,005 on Monday.
The baht fell to a low of 32.40 to the dollar on Monday from 31.90 at midday and 31.75 near the Friday close.
A Reuters survey of 11 banks around the region found the average forecast for the baht at the end of the year was 32.64. The estimates ranged from 30.00 to 35.00.
Brokers said the stock market turnover was partly thinned by a holiday in Hong Kong on Monday.

Most key sectors retreated with banks leading the decline by shedding 5.33 percent. Bangkok Bank topped the active list, losing eight baht to 160, Thai Farmers Bank fell six to 103, and Siam Commercial Bank tumbled 10 to 116.
